questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Some methods were preferable, others not. 
Preferable methods: Memorisation of complete poems, regular testing of your understanding of presented ideas.
Less preferable: One teacher from the political faculty just read out loud for the class for 2 hours every time.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easier than you should think. It takes a couple of months, but now i dont want to leave.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just speak and have fun! People are wonderful here

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None. Cultural differences, though they exist, are more of a grey zone than a solid difference in understanding.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nobility of the culture. Moldova is more conservative (I'm not speaking politically). Manners, helpfulness, and elegance are valued here. It really doesn't differ much from Denmark. Only the expression is different

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It's okay to feel the weight of the spoken level in Moldova. You are surrounded by native speakers. Keep up your motivation.

questions.answer: To create a new life detached from everything known.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
